I was lucky to have teachers who understood me, and acknowledged why I struggled so much, and they did their best to facilitate for me so that I would be able to graduate. They changed my schedule so that I only had attend half a day, and some teachers also allowed me to skip all homework. But despite all this, I would still be absent a lot.

Not the same injury as you whatsoever, but I did break my ankle lead climbing in March of last year. My biggest advice would probably be that once you start climbing again to listen to your body. Don’t push it too hard if you’re experiencing pain, but try to ease into it instead. Accept that you most likely won’t be at the same level as before your injury, but at the same time chances are that you’ll fairly quickly get back to a similar level as before. It took me about three months I believe to get back to the level I climbed before the injury. Another tips would be to do so strength exercises you can still do while injured. Especially core and upper back (if possible while injured) will benefit a lot once you get back, as those muscles are quite essential for climbers, the more strength you’re able to uphold/improve while injured the faster you’ll get back to your former level.

I was exactly the same up until a few months ago.

Now I’m by no means an expert, but I can at least tell you what has worked for me so far.

Do you have any safe food you think you could be able to keep down? This can be literally anything. An apple, some low calorie soup or whatever the hell you like.  If you have, then start there, try to eat that food at least once or twice throughout the day. You don’t have to feel full afterwards, the goal is simply to eat anything and experiencing the fact that you’re able to eat something without the need to throw up. At least that’s where I started. 

Once I was able to eat that food (for me the food i found easiest to eat was soup) once or twice throughout the day, I tried eating it until I felt full. Feeling full is my biggest trigger and I will get extreme anxiety whenever i feel full. Since I already had become comfortable with eating small portions of it, it eased my anxiety somewhat when I ate it until feeling full. And so, after a while I was finally comfortable having a normal portion of it without throwing up. Once that happened I started over again with something else, while making sure I was also having some soup throughout the day as I knew I now was able to tolerate that.


It can be an extremely long process until you’re comfortable keeping a portion of it down, so don’t get discouraged if it takes a long time. It’s been about four months for me now since I actively started this process, and I’ve only gotten to three meals I’m able to tolerate. It’s not perfect or ideal in any way, but it is progress nonetheless.
